key_insight: Averaging over grain orientations extends thermodynamic dislocation theory to general stress/strain states and produces an associated J2 plasticity law whose hardening comes from dislocation kinetics rather than empirical fitting.
engineering_relevance: This gives a single physics-based constitutive model that can predict tension, compression, and torsion across wide temperature and strain-rate ranges for use in metal forming and dynamic loading simulations.
method: Use equal-probability grain-orientation averaging to define mean resolved shear stress and strain.
Apply isotropic orientation identities to link mean shear stress to von Mises stress and plastic flow to the stress deviator.
Evolve dislocation density and effective disorder temperature in time to follow arbitrary loading paths and compute torque–twist directly.
evidence_signal: The model is calibrated for copper using 142 data points from Hopkinson-bar tension, dynamic compression, and torque–twist tests, matching response from room temperature to 1173 K and 10 to 2300 s^-1 within about 6% rms.
watch_item: The predictions depend on the assumed initial dislocation state, which is especially important for explaining the tension–torsion discrepancy.
paper_title: Averaging in thermodynamic dislocation theory: general macroscopically uniform stress and strain states
